keyRule: `keyDistinct`/`keyMin`/`keyMax`/`keyDensity` describe the table's f0 id space, measured from the decoded rows. Density is the share of the integers between min and max that are real ids - the closer to 1.0, the more readily any column of small integers will appear to join to it.
note: Every column of every table in the client: the type the decode inferred, the evidence it inferred it from, and the distribution of the values. One line per table - the column detail is nested inside it, so this file stays under the 5,000-line rule and `json.load` gives an agent the whole layer's shape in one read. Column names are positional (f0..fN) because nothing in this repo knows what they mean. Load this file, do not grep it: a table's line carries all of its columns and can run to hundreds of KB. CATALOG.md and raw/_catalog/strings.json are the views built for grep.
sampleRule: `samples` appears only on columns inferred as strings. Every column has a string-hypothesis decode recorded in its colinfo, but on an int column those bytes are not content and must not be read as any.

columnDetail.name: f55
samples: Melee heroes are masters of close-quarters combat, relying on their weapons to unleash savage attacks. From knights and rogues to lancers, barbarians, and monks, they weave through enemies and strike with unmatched force and precision. Melee fighters excel at delivering raw, powerful blows and can sometimes cleave through multiple foes at once. Always on the front lines, these warriors embody the essence of ferocity and skill, turning the tide of battle with relentless attacks and unwavering resolve.

Magic heroes weave the mystical arts into all manner of destructive and defensive spells. They excel at dealing damage to both single targets and large groups, raining fire, frost, arcane, nature, shadow, or holy damage upon their foes. While most Magic heroes prefer to remain at a distance, many have found ways to channel their spellcraft into powerful defensive spells, using their Mana as a means to defend against harm. Whether acting as a Wizard or an indomitable Mage Knight, Magic heroes are forces of destruction on the battlefield.

Hybrid heroes have mastered the art of martial and magical combat, becoming spellswords. They seamlessly blend their mage-craft into dazzling displays of close-range fighting, infusing elemental might into their weapons, cleaving through foes with frozen blades, or even using shadow magic to enhance their assassination abilities. Some Hybrid augment their fighting capabilities with a single element, while others use powerful manipulative and control spells to become better warriors.

Pure Healers focus entirely on restoring and rejuvenating allies. Able to not only heal and resurrect, but also shield and prevent damage entirely, Pure Healers devote their attention and mana more to their party than to enemies. Using powerful direct heals, buffs, and control spells, they keep their party strong and moving forward.

Combat Healers seamlessly weave back and forth between healing allies and damaging enemies: oftentimes doing both simultaneously. Many Combat Healers heal by siphoning life from foes and giving it to their allies. Others build up power by healing to unleash devastating spells on enemies. While not as potent as their Pure Healer counterparts, Combat Healers make up for it by assisting in dealing damage and slaying enemies faster.

columnDetail.name: f53
samples:
Tanks are indomitable bulwarks that absorb and deflect damage, taking hits so that the rest of the party stays safe. They are the vanguard of any group, using shields, heavy armor, monstrous transform effects, and sometimes even raw agility to block, dodge, parry, and shrug off incoming effects. With high health and defensive abilities, Tanks hold foes’ attention while the rest of the party does their job.
Healers are powerful spellcasters that wield their magic to bolster and rejuvenate allies. Able to buff, restore, and even resurrect fallen friends, most Healers are students of either the Holy Light or the eternal cycle of Nature. Some healers even weave these elements into more offensive schools, wielding holy cauterizing fire or soothing allies with frozen heals. With large pools of magic and an array of supportive spells, they are the backbone of their party, ensuring everyone can charge forward into danger.
Barbaric fighters, agile assassins, and powerful wizards all share a common goal: swiftly disposing of their enemies. Whether through a mighty storm of steel or a torrent or arcane magic, those who focus on slaying foes are known as Damage Dealers (DPS). This role encompasses the widest variety of Heroes: from wandering knights to rangers, thieves, and sorcerers. To walk this path is to embrace destruction.

samples:
Manastorm Spells are unique, powerful abilities designed to help you navigate and survive the chaos of the Manastorm. These spells offer a wide range of effects such as bonus stats, crowd control, or utility, that can turn the tide of battle or provide crucial support in challenging scenarios.

You can equip up to four spells at a time, known as your 'Active Manastorm Spells'. These spells can be swapped out to suit your playstyle, role, or the specific challenge you're facing. You can view all of your acquired Manastorm Spells in your Spellbook, under the Ascension Manastorm Items tab.

Each spell can upgrade up to eight different ranks. Higher ranks provide significantly more powerful effects, improving damage, healing, stats, or duration, based on the spell type. Upgrading your spells is essential for keeping pace with the increasing difficulty of Manastorm content.

You can use Bonzo Bolts get new spells or upgrade existing ones from Cogsworth.

Marks of Ascension are a Currency earned from virtually every type of content in the game including PvP encounters, finishing a quest, or completing a dungeon or raid. These tokens are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and serve as one of the primary ways to progress and refine your character.

Marks of Ascension can be spent at Nozdormu, found in your Capital City, where they can be exchanged for a wide selection of items. These include ability purges, talent purges, and Mystic Enchanting materials which can help you reset or fine-tune your build. You can also buy high-level gear, heirlooms, and other essential tools to enhance your power or level up faster.

Each time you reforge one of your Mystic Scrolls at an Enchanting Altar, you earn Mystic Enchanting Experience. Gaining enough experience will increase your Mystic Enchanting level, which rewards you with a Mystic Extract used to permanently add an enchant to your collection.

You can track your experience progress directly at any Enchanting Altar. Mystic Enchanting levels are realm-wide, meaning all your characters on the same server contribute to and share the same level progression.

Marks of Ascension are a Currency earned from many types of content including PvP encounters, finishing quests, or completing dungeons and raids. These tokens are stored in your Currency panel (Hotkey C -> Currency Tab) and serve as one of the primary ways to progress and refine your character. On Wildcard, Marks of Ascension can be used at Silas Darkmoon for Scrolls of Fortune and Skill Card Packs. Marks can also be spent at other key vendors for gear, Heirlooms, and other progression tools that help you catch up or strengthen your character.

Enchanting Altars allow you to obtain, collect, and apply thousands of potential Mystic Enchants to achieve your maximum power! 

You can discover altars in the open world by finding an enchanting altar symbol on your World Map. Altars can also be summoned by your fellow players for a short duration, most often in your Capital City and other major quest hubs. 

Summonable enchanting altars can be obtained from the Auction House for gold or purchased from the Ascension Store for Donation Points (DP).

versionRule: One version per DISTINCT sha256 among the copies of a path, not one per carrying archive: byte-identical copies in several archives are ONE version, listed once under the highest-ranked archive that carries those bytes with the rest recorded in `alsoIn`. The chain winner keeps its place at raw/tables/<T>/ and is listed with `chainWinner` true; every other version is decoded into raw/tables/<T>/variants/<slug>/ by the same decoder, so the two are comparable byte for byte. `rowDelta` is this version's record count minus the chain winner's. A chain context is a set of archives a running client actually loads, enumerated from the client's own directory layout rather than from a list: `baseChain` is every archive in the base and locale directories - what a character reads when no realm overlay applies - and there is one further context per realm directory found, holding that same base set plus the archives that realm's `listarchive` declares. A version APPLIES TO a context when its archive is the highest-ranked carrier of that path inside it. A version that is the highest-ranked carrier in no context at all is still decoded - it is real client data - and is marked shadowed.
